title: A puff of air: /p/ and /b/
goal: Practise /p/ and /b/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Close both lips, then release them. At the start of a stressed word, p usually has a stronger puff than b. Hold a tissue a little in front of your mouth; do not force your breath.
spelling: p and b can change a word's meaning. A final p or b does not need an extra vowel.

dialogue.name: Echo
dialogue.text: Yes, please pass it to me.

task: Ask someone to pass a pen. Keep the final sound of “pen” clear without adding a syllable.

cards.title: How to make it clear
sections: For both /p/ and /b/, close both lips briefly, then release. A stressed initial /p/ usually has a stronger puff than /b/. Do not bite the lower lip as for /v/, or add “uh” after either stop.
Use a mirror if helpful. Keep your jaw and throat comfortable. Stop if the movement hurts; do not force it.

articulation.label: pat
articulation.alt: pat: /p/ → /æ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
